title: 2 km or Zero? Displacement Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
Aarav rides to a shop one kilometre away and comes straight back. His trip meter says 2 km, his physics teacher says he moved zero. Both are right. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 2, Motion in a Straight Line) we compare distance and displacement side by side.

Watch one bicycle ride on a straight road with a live readout and a graph: distance keeps climbing while displacement falls after the turn. We write the rule step by step (s = total path, Δx = x_f - x_i, |Δx| ≤ s), show link by link why distance can never be smaller, and test it on a circle at a quarter, half and full turn. Then a worked half-lap example, the 2πr exam trap, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 Two trips back to the start
0:29 Distance and displacement: what they are
0:52 Live sim: one ride, two numbers
1:33 The rule, step by step
2:05 Why distance is never smaller
2:34 Side by side + pause and think
3:06 Test it on a circle
3:51 Worked example: half a round park
4:24 Exam trap: one full round
4:46 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:24 Recap and three questions

Next episode: Speed and Velocity. Two cyclists at the same speed in opposite directions: same speed, but different velocity?
